text:
mira: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: hybrid/office logistics. Dropping clarifications here so folks can find them later. I'll turn this into a short FAQ.

jon: Two quick ones: 1) If I need to fly out for a multi-day tech offsite, can I buy refundable tickets? 2) Are partners allowed at evening social dinners?

hr-lead: Refundable tickets are allowed when the event is mission-critical and dates are uncertain; include justification and manager approval on the expense. For routine team offsites, book standard refundable vs non-refundable depending on price delta. Partners: allowed only for informal regional socials; not allowed at customer-facing or strategy retreats unless pre-approved.

people-ops-bot: Travel protocol doc updated: https://intranet.redwood/policies/travel_v3 (edited)

jon: If I plan a "work from a different city" week (US only, <10 days), is that automatic approval? Any forms?

hr-lead: Submit the Remote Location Request at least 3 business days before. For US travel under 14 days we generally approve; cross-border requires finance/legal. If your work requires access to internal systems from a different region, request VPN exception early.

infra-eng: Any changes to office hoteling? I had a recurring desk reservation that vanished after a calendar update.

hr-lead: We're rolling an improved hoteling system next month to reduce conflicts. Current priority: scheduled meetings > recurring desk owners > single-day hoteling. If you hit a conflict, file a #desk-ops ticket and ops will reconcile.

mira: What's the budget guidance for manager-organized small offsites (<3 days)?

hr-lead: Default per-person cap $300/day covering lodging, meals, and local transit. Submit an Offsite Budget Request if you expect to exceed that. For hiring/offsite interview days, separate budget applies.

jon: Childcare coverage? If I have to travel for mandatory training, can I get childcare reimbursed?

hr-lead: Childcare reimbursement for mandatory company travel is considered case-by-case; managers must pre-approve and people-ops processes the reimbursement with receipts. Routine childcare not covered.

people-ops-bot: Coworking stipend info: $150/month opt-in; day-pass reimbursements up to $30/day for short trips with receipts. https://intranet.redwood/benefits/coworking (pinned)

ceo: Leadership note: For any customer or partner visits to our data centers or Sensitive infra sites, request visitor access at least 72 hours in advance; security will not process walk-ins.

jon: If someone brings a medical accommodation (service animal), is that covered?

hr-lead: Service animals are supported and fees deemed reasonable will be covered. Non-service pets not covered unless an approved accommodation. Work with HR for documentation.

mira: Thanks all. I'll make a one-page cheat sheet with flowcharts (workation vs remote request, guest rules, expense examples) and ping this channel when live. Volunteers to review wording?

infra-eng: I can review the security/infra visit flow.

people-ops-bot: FAQ draft uploaded to all-hands resources: https://intranet.redwood/allhands/jun-2026/faq (edited)
